reasons: Deviation classification is correct: Article IV imposes a 36-month Initial Period and the document's only termination rights are Licensor-side or fault/insolvency/change-of-control based, so there is no Customer convenience right at all — this fails even the fallback (60–90 days' notice exit) and sits in walk-away territory under T4C.

The redline is minimal and additive: it inserts a new subsection IV into the term article granting Licensee a 30-day convenience termination with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and confirms Licensor has no convenience right during the term, tracking the rule's model language without disturbing existing text.
No Vendor convenience right exists, so no deletion was required; the added no-Licensor-convenience sentence is consistent with the preferred position and does not create a new burden on us.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the correct voice, cites the playbook position (customer exit required in terms over 12 months) and offers the 60–90 day fallback.

The failed 'Customer convenience termination present' check appears to be a phrasing/alias artifact (the clause uses 'Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience ... upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice'), not a substantive gap.
